title: ENTRY live monitoring as the demotion signal (not an edge lever): live ENTRY closes vs the dev/held-out band, rule written before use
note: RULE (written before the first live read, operator 2026-11-01: ENTRY goes live on bybit_2 as approved). Expected band from dev/held-out: traded-5 -0.041 net R per decision (dev, 4 seeds, n about 5.5k each); pooled frozen-60 +0.007 (dev and held-out); October 2026 -0.019R (manager). Evaluate realised net R per closed ENTRY decision (full cost stack: fees, slippage, funding) per account over ALL its closed ENTRY trades, every 50 closes once n >= 100. FLAG ENTRY_LIVE_NEGATIVE when mean + 2*SE < 0 (SE = SD/sqrt(n)): the live loss is statistically real. FLAG ENTRY_LIVE_BELOW_DEV when mean < -0.041 - 2*SE: worse than even the weak traded-5 dev reading. A flag is a realtime ping to the operator with the numbers; it demotes nothing by itself (no halting; a demotion is the mirror-window rule's, and the operator's). Reads only closed trades; sizes nothing. Tier 2 because it adds a standing read on the live ENTRY legs. Gates this adds: none (a flag, not a switch).

observation.what: the live ENTRY (bybit_2 + bybit_portfolio) realised net R per closed decision, after fees and funding, is read on a standing cadence against the band below and a flag is raised by the rule
observation.how_to_check: the demotion read for the ENTRY legs on /api/bot (mirror net-of-cost window)

writeback.arch: none until the monitor reads a new field
